sections.label: COE price increases and supply
sections.summary: The speaker says measures would contain COE price increases and fluctuation, notes this month's Cat A and B premia of $119,000 and $136,000, and urges more aggressive cutting of future supply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These would, in my view, contribute to containing COE price increases, as well as its fluctuation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Such moves are even more salient today, as this month's Cat A and B premia cleared eye-watering amounts of $119,000 and $136,000, respectively.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since that time, the Ministry has rolled out the cut-and-fill system, which seeks to balance out the year-to-year variations in COE supply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am, nevertheless, gratified that at least some steps have been taken to manage the feast-and-famine nature of year-to-year COE pricing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to be more aggressive in its cutting from future supply and not be satisfied with mainly moving guaranteed de-registrations.

sections.label: Disabled Persons Scheme COE waiver
sections.summary: A Disabled Persons Scheme grants a full waiver of the COE if a disabled person is seeking a vehicle to commute to work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, in one specific case, the disabled, we, and I cannot emphasise enough, already have in place a programme, the Disabled Persons Scheme, that grants a full waiver of the COE, if a disabled person is seeking a vehicle to commute to work.

sections.label: COE discounts for disabled and parents
sections.summary: The disabled get a 100% COE discount, and parents of two or more children, at least two below 14, get 10% for each additional child beyond the first.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For the disabled: we offer a 100% discount on the COE.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For parents of two or more children, of which at least two must be below 14 years: a 10% discount for each additional child beyond the first.

sections.label: Discount for primary caregivers
sections.summary: Primary caregivers of two parents above 80, or one parent with a chronic illness needing regular checkups, all in the same household, get a 10% discount.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For primary caregivers of either two parents above 80 years of age, or one parent who suffers from a chronic illness that is in need of regular medical checkups, all of whom must live within the same household: a 10% discount.

sections.label: Eligibility criteria and car ownership costs
sections.summary: The discount may apply to families earning below the median income threshold or exclude the top quintile of earners, as the Government de-emphasises car ownership costs and foregrounds road usage costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, we may apply the discount apply to families that earn below the median income threshold, or instead, we may exclude the top quintile of earners from this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government is moving towards a system where the costs of car ownership will be de-emphasised while that of road usage would come to the fore.

sections.label: COE revenues and public spending
sections.summary: COE revenues of about $4 billion to 6 billion a year on average subsidise public transport and other Government expenditures like healthcare, education and defence.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The COE revenues, which are about $4 billion to 6 billion a year on average, go towards subsidising public transport as well as other Government expenditures for the good of society like healthcare, education and defence.

sections.label: COE supply stabilisation measures
sections.summary: The Government brought forward COE quota, made a one-off injection of up to about 20,000 COEs, and quarterly supply has doubled since 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The Government has tried to stabilise the supply.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We brought forward some COE quota from the future to flatten the peaks and troughs of the supply curve and we are making a one-off injection of up to about 20,000 COEs, which we announced in October 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: In fact, the COE quarterly supply has doubled since 2023.

sections.label: Bus and train operational subsidies
sections.summary: The Government spends some $2 billion yearly on operational subsidies to keep bus and train services running.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The Government spends some $2 billion on operational subsidies to keep our bus and train services running every year.

sections.label: COE needs-based system rejected
sections.summary: The Government says a needs-based COE system is subjective, divisive and benefits too few, while the market mechanism is fairest and most effective.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: A needs-based system for the COE sounds attractive, but in practice, it is subjective, divisive and benefits too few.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The market mechanism is transparent and allows the Government to channel COE revenues to the benefit of the wider public.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This is not the perfect system, but it is the fairest and most effective way to allocate a scarce resource in Singapore's context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.30 am.
